normalized.recommendation: Decision today: decline Parcelbird Now, fund the software hires and review the four conditions each year

alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected: needs $9.5M to month 18, 27% gross margin, no observed site profitable after site costs, leaves about 6 months of runway (half the floor), competes with the grocers it sells to.
Chosen: needs $1.2M to month 18, 81% gross margin, proven ARR growing 60% a year, keeps the runway floor, serves grocers that want their own fast delivery; beats Parcelbird Now on all five tests.

Four conditions would justify reopening: positive site contribution for a full quarter, retained customers repay acquisition within a year, cash after capex covers 12-month runway floor, rider pay rules settled in Columbus, Indianapolis and Kansas City; review each year.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: Board confidential; synthetic benchmark data from the briefing pack
The pack has no regional split, so 'nobody owns the Midwest' cannot be tested with this data
Minimum pay standards under discussion in two of the three cities would raise rider time cost
Survey and pop-up measure different groups (residents aged 25–39 against acquired customers); the comparison is indicative
Payback: orders in the first two months from customers who later lapse are ignored; they would shorten payback a little
Payback: no churn after month three; any further churn makes payback longer
Payback uses the plan's $2.02 per order, which needs every input beyond the best site
The pack does not say whether the $9.5M includes the software business's own burn; the chart takes the generous reading that it does
The $9.5M assumes contribution profit by month 18; at benchmark economics losses keep running
If the $9.5M excludes today's burn: another $7.2M over 18 months would leave the company $4.7M short
Lead investor calls a new round for a delivery operator unlikely
Nine-store estimate: all nine stores run at the median of the 14 customer sites on every input, at steady state; launch marketing, capex and head-office costs come on top
Software breakeven: revenue taken as ARR and burn as costs net of revenue; costs other than cost of revenue stay flat apart from the $0.8M of hires
next_steps: Decline the Parcelbird Now proposal and record the four conditions for reopening it — Board — January 2027
Hire two engineers and two sales staff for the software business — Founders — Q1 2027
Close the nine late-stage grocers and package a fast-delivery offer for pipeline grocers — Head of sales — H1 2027
Report contribution, retention and rider pay at customer sites against the four conditions — Founders — Quarterly from Q2 2027
normalized.extraction_notes: The deck came as plain text with no images. On slide 15 the stacked chart has a 'base' series (0; 6.6; 2.5; 0) that is a waterfall offset, so only the 'Cash' series values are recorded as evidence. On slide 13 the deck shows the payback formula with ÷ symbols between all four inputs; it is copied as written. On slides 10 and 20 some table cells contain two phrases separated by '/' ('Hardest to reach / ...', 'The board's hard rule / ...'), which look like a label followed by text. Slide-number footers, the section navigation bars, and the slide 1 subtitle, author, audience and date lines are left out of the claims.
